The wheel $L$ makes 4 full turns when $K$ makes 5 full turns; also $L$ makes 6 full turns when $M$ makes 7 full turns. <image1> The perimeter of wheel $M$ is $30 \mathrm{~cm}$. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three pulleys, the smaller wheel on the left is labeled K, the larger wheel above in the middle is labeled L, and the smaller wheel on the right is labeled M. A belt connects K and L, and also connects L and M, indicating that these wheels are driven by belts and there is no slipping. Reasoning: When there is no slipping, the length traveled by the same belt in the same amount of time is the same, so for two connected wheels, “number of rotations × circumference” is equal. K and L: when K turns 5 revolutions, L turns 4 revolutions, therefore 5P_K = 4P_L. L and M: when L turns 6 revolutions, M turns 7 revolutions, therefore 6P_L = 7P_M. It is known that P_M = 30 cm, so 6P_L = 7 × 30 = 210, giving P_L = 35 cm. Substituting again into 5P_K = 4P_L gives 5P_K = 4 × 35 = 140, therefore P_K = 28 cm.

method.method_draft: First read the image as a belt system with three labeled wheels: small wheel K on the left, large wheel L in the middle/top, and small wheel M on the right, with belts connecting K to L and L to M. From the text, take the two no-slip rotation facts: when K makes 5 turns, L makes 4 turns; when M makes 7 turns, L makes 6 turns; also P_M=30 cm. Use the no-slip rule that for a belt-connected pair over the same time, number of turns times wheel perimeter is equal. Thus for K and L: 5P_K=4P_L. For L and M: 6P_L=7P_M. Substitute P_M=30 to get P_L=35, then P_K=(4/5)P_L=28 cm.
